Macrons

Consonantal i

Household, washing & chores

clean the house verb

also cleaning, clean up

classical

M-O s.v. clean house
Cato
Plautus

munditiās facere

Examples

  • nē cessētur, munditiās facitō

    no idling: clean (Cato on a rainy day)Cato, Agr. 39.2

  • munditiās volō fierī; ecferte hūc scōpās

    I want the place cleaned; bring the brooms out herePlaut. Stich. 2.2.22, as cited by Lewis & Short

See also chore, tidy up, broom, clean.

SourcesLewis & Short: munditia

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. clean house, clean up, tidy up, broom: dustpan, garbage, trash, garbage can, waste basket. John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): pp. 38, 39, 290, 292, 307, 320, 401, 404.

Cato, Livy and Petronius from the Latinitas loci collections; Plautus as cited by L&S (edition spelling ecferte kept).
